title: House Passes $70B ICE/CBP Funding Package 214-212 on Party-Line Vote — Sends Bill to Trump's Desk
detail: On June 9, 2026, the U.S. House of Representatives voted 214-212 along near-party-line lines to pass the $70 billion immigration enforcement reconciliation package after the Senate approved it 52-47 on June 5. The bill provides approximately $38.5 billion for ICE to hire, pay, and train personnel over three years — including $7 billion for Homeland Security Investigations agents — plus $22.6 billion for CBP hiring, training, and equipment, $3.5 billion for border technology, and roughly $5 billion in discretionary DHS enforcement funds. Passage ended a four-month lapse in dedicated immigration-enforcement funding and capped a fight that had exposed tensions between President Trump and congressional Republicans over the bill's $1.776 billion anti-weaponization settlement fund for Trump political allies. No Democrats voted for the bill. The legislation funds ICE and CBP operations through the remainder of Trump's second term, insulating both agencies from future government-shutdown fights, and now heads to the White House for the president's signature.
